newsitem.title: USA: Labor's Hamel sees overstatement in US Feb payroll.
newsitem.headline: Labor's Hamel sees overstatement in US Feb payroll.

text.p: Labor Department economist Harvey Hamel on Friday said that the 339,000 increase in U.S. February non-farm payrolls was a solid number although it be slightly overstated.
Interviewed on Reuters Financial Television, Hamel also said that it was unlikely that the unexpected jump in construction jobs in the month could be sustained.

"That (339,000) figure is solid," he said, "(although) "I would say that if you look at the details there may be some slight overstatement in that the biggest gainer in February was the construction industry...(and) that was attributable to the mild weather across the country."
He said this contrasted with severe weather in January that had restricted employment growth.
Hamel said that construction employment, which rose 109,000 in February, has been strong since the end of 1995 although it had not been gaining by the kind of numbers that it showed last month.
"What it is telling me is that although construction is strong, it's not strong to the degree of 109,000 a month."
